svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
Juice Shop · 20.1.1 · 7 components · 20 data flows · 5 trust boundaries · 64 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-02; tb-2 External → C-04; tb-3 External → C-03; tb-8 C-02 → External; tb-9 C-05 → External

df-002: SPA requests static assets and public REST routes (unauthenticated) (HTTP) df-012: POST /rest/chat — user message to LLM chatbot endpoint (HTTP) df-018: POST /rest/user/data-export — authenticated user requests GDPR data export (HTTP) df-002 authentication: no authentication check on public routes including /api-docs, /metrics, /file-upload; evidence: server.ts:309, server.ts:286 df-012 authentication: No authentication check; confirmed by T-052 (evidence-verified); evidence: server.ts:607 df-018 authentication: No authentication check; confirmed by T-052 (evidence-verified); evidence: server.ts:607

df-003: POST /rest/user/login — user submits email and password to obtain JWT (HTTP) df-004: POST /rest/user/login via OAuth-derived credentials after Google profile lookup (HTTP) df-003 authentication: email + password submitted in request body; server issues RS256 JWT on success; evidence: routes/login.ts:34, lib/insecurity.ts:54 df-003 access group: Login methods; alternatives; step n/a df-004 authentication: frontend extracts Google access_token from URL fragment (implicit flow), calls Google userinfo, derives email-based password, then POSTs to /rest/user/login; evidence: frontend/src/app/oauth/oauth.component.ts:46, frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148 df-004 access group: Login methods; alternatives; step n/a

df-005: POST /rest/2fa/verify — submit TOTP token with temporary JWT to complete 2FA login (HTTP) df-005 authentication: temporary JWT issued at first login step; TOTP code verified against stored totpSecret; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:17, routes/2fa.ts:31

df-006: POST /rest/user/reset-password — reset password using security question answer (HTTP) df-006 authentication: security question answer; no bearer token required at this endpoint; evidence: routes/resetPassword.ts:16

df-007: Authenticated REST API calls with JWT bearer token (user-level) (HTTP) df-007 authentication: RS256 JWT in Authorization header or localStorage; express-jwt middleware validates on protected routes; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:84, frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:13
df-008: SQL query for user credential lookup during login (SQL) df-008 authentication: in-process Sequelize call; no network authentication; evidence: routes/login.ts:34

df-009: Sequelize ORM CRUD operations for users, products, orders, and challenge state (SQL) df-009 authentication: in-process Sequelize call to embedded SQLite file; no network authentication; evidence: models/user.ts:36
df-010: MarsDB embedded calls for product review and order document queries (embedded-db) df-010 authentication: in-process MarsDB library call; no network layer; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9

df-011: WebSocket connection for real-time challenge-solved notifications (WebSocket) df-011 authentication: No authentication check; confirmed by T-033 (evidence-verified); evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23

df-013: LLM inference request (OpenAI-compatible) with user-supplied prompt (HTTPS) df-013 authentication: LLM_API_KEY environment variable; absent for Ollama (local model); evidence: routes/chat.ts:110

df-017: Ethereum WebSocket RPC connection to listen for NFTMinted events and verify wallets (WebSocket) df-017 authentication: provider URL from configuration; no explicit auth scheme found in source; evidence: routes/nftMint.ts:23

df-019: POST / (data erasure form with cookie session) — GDPR data erasure request (HTTP) df-019 authentication: session cookie validated in routes/dataErasure.ts:76; evidence: routes/dataErasure.ts:76

Human end-user operating a web browser. May be anonymous (unauthenticated) or authenticated with a standard or admin account.
Google OAuth 2.0 authorization server. The Angular login page redirects here (implicit flow); the returned access token is used to fetch the Google user profile, then derive app credentials.
OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (Ollama or remote provider) invoked by the /rest/chat route. Endpoint URL and API key supplied via LLM_API_URL and LLM_API_KEY environment variables.
Ethereum JSON-RPC / WebSocket provider used by the NFT minting challenge to listen for on-chain NFTMinted events and verify wallet ownership.
g.text: provider used by the NFT minting

g.title: Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.

Google OAuth 2.0 df-014: Browser redirect to Google OAuth authorization endpoint (implicit flow) (HTTPS); client_id and response_type=token in authorization request; no state parameter present (CSRF risk); token returned in URL fragment df-015: Google OAuth redirect back with access_token in URL fragment (HTTPS); Completes the sign-in: the provider returns its result to the client's registered redirect URI df-016: GET https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v1/userinfo — fetch Google profile with access_token (HTTPS); Google access_token appended as query parameter to userinfo endpoint

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.

The recipient checks the token supplied with the request.

The caller presents a configured service credential.

security question answer; no bearer token required at this endpoint

Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
